title: Counting particles by mass: the mole
summary: The mole links the number of particles to measurable masses and volumes. Use molar mass, find empirical and molecular formulas, and work with concentrations of solutions.

keyterms.definition: The amount of substance containing exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities (atoms, molecules, ions…).
The number of particles per mole: 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
The mass of one mole of a substance in g mol⁻¹; numerically equal to its relative formula mass.
Sum of the relative atomic masses of all atoms in a formula; it has no units.
The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule; a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula.
Amount (or mass) of solute per unit volume of solution, usually in mol dm⁻³ or g dm⁻³.
A homogeneous mixture of a solute dissolved in a solvent.
A solution whose concentration is accurately known, made in a volumetric flask.
Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of particles.
The percentage by mass of each element in a compound.

questions.prompt: How many moles are in 9.00 g of water (M = 18.02 g mol⁻¹)?

questions.text: The number of molecules in 2.00 mol of CO₂ is ___ × 10²⁴.

questions.statement: The relative formula mass of a substance has units of g mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Mr is a ratio and has no units; molar mass M has units g mol⁻¹ and the same numerical value.

questions.prompt: A compound is 40.0 % C, 6.7 % H and 53.3 % O by mass. What is its empirical formula?

questions.text: A compound with empirical formula CH₂ has Mr = 56. Its molecular formula is ___.
questions.explanation: Empirical mass of CH₂ ≈ 14; 56/14 = 4, so the molecular formula is C₄H₈.

questions.prompt: Match each quantity to its unit.
questions.explanation: Keeping units in working is the best way to check a calculation.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are in 0.10 mol of NH₃?
questions.explanation: Each NH₃ has 4 atoms: 0.10 × 4 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 2.4 × 10²³.

questions.statement: Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and ethanoic acid (C₂H₄O₂) have the same empirical formula.
questions.explanation: Both simplify to CH₂O.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to find an empirical formula from percentage composition.
items: Assume 100 g so each % becomes a mass in g
Divide each mass by its Ar to get moles
Divide all mole values by the smallest
Multiply to whole numbers if needed
questions.explanation: Moles give the atom ratio; dividing by the smallest gives the simplest ratio.

questions.prompt: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in NH₄NO₃ (Mr = 80.06)?
What is the concentration of a solution with 0.200 mol NaOH in 500 cm³?
questions.explanation: Convert to dm³: 500 cm³ = 0.500 dm³. c = n/V = 0.200 / 0.500 = 0.400 mol dm⁻³.

questions.text: Moles of HCl in 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ acid = ___ mol.

questions.statement: A standard solution is prepared in a volumetric flask.
questions.explanation: Volumetric flasks hold one accurate volume, so the concentration is known precisely.

questions.prompt: 10.0 cm³ of 2.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl is diluted to 100.0 cm³. The new concentration is…
questions.explanation: Moles stay the same: c₁V₁ = c₂V₂ → 2.00 × 10.0 = c₂ × 100.0 → c₂ = 0.200 mol dm⁻³.

questions.text: A 0.50 mol dm⁻³ NaCl solution (M = 58.44 g mol⁻¹) has a mass concentration of ___ g dm⁻³.
questions.explanation: 0.50 mol dm⁻³ × 58.44 g mol⁻¹ = 29.2 g dm⁻³.

questions.prompt: Match each component to its role.
questions.explanation: Aqueous (aq) solutions have water as the solvent.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to make 250.0 cm³ of a standard solution from a solid.
items: Dissolve it in a small volume of distilled water in a beaker
Transfer to a volumetric flask with rinsings
Add water up to the graduation mark
questions.explanation: Rinsings ensure all the solute is transferred; filling to the mark gives the exact volume.

questions.statement: By Avogadro's law, 1 mol of H₂ and 1 mol of CO₂ occupy the same volume at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.explanation: Gas volume depends on the number of particles, not their identity (for ideal gases).

questions.prompt: What mass of CuSO₄ (M = 159.6 g mol⁻¹) is needed for 250 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ solution?

questions.explanation: Divide volumes in cm³ by 1000 to convert to dm³.
